name: Montana
summary: Statutes, constitution and the court rules that the Legislature codifies (M. R. Civ. P., M. R. Evid., M. R. App. P., Uniform District Court Rules, all in MCA Titles 25-26) are on mca.legmt.gov as one short HTML page per section, with a deterministic zero-padded URL; fetch_doc.py reads them, WebFetch is gated for built URLs, and Justia (2025 MCA) is a WebFetch-only tier-2 fallback. Other court rules are full-set PDFs on courts.mt.gov that WebFetch truncates (civil rules stop at Rule 23.1). The ARM and the Montana Administrative Register live in a JavaScript app (rules.mt.gov, UUID URLs), so text comes from Cornell LII per rule. Case law is the weak spot: the Supreme Court docket (supremecourtdocket.mt.gov) is an Angular app and the State Law Library's searchcourts.mt.gov is unreachable, so opinions are read on Justia (constructible from year + docket) and linked by public-domain citation (YYYY MT N, since 1998); Workers' Compensation Court decisions are year-listed PDFs on courts.mt.gov.

citation_map.notes: Montana's own statute style puts the code name AFTER the section ('§ 27-2-204, MCA' or '27-2-204, MCA'); Bluebook is 'Mont. Code Ann. § 27-2-204'. Section numbers are always title-chapter-section with a 3- or 4-digit last element, and a chapter may carry a letter (30-9A-101); the statute regex requires an MCA / Mont. Code Ann. / 'Montana Code' marker, so bare hyphenated numbers (shared with many states) never route here. Ranges ('§§ 27-2-201 through 27-2-205, MCA') capture the first section (group section4); the (?![\d-]) guard keeps a range from being read as one hyphenated number. Court rules: law_aliases map the rule sets to the MCA title-chapter that hosts them (25-20 civil, 26-10 evidence, 25-21 appellate, 25-19 Uniform District Court Rules). Criminal procedure is statutory (MCA Title 46), cited as sections, not rules. Bare 'Rule 12(b)(6)' or 'Rule 702' is not routed here. Case citations: the Dec. 16, 1997 order (courts.mt.gov/external/library/docs/cite_cases.pdf) created 'YYYY MT N' with ¶ numbering from Jan. 1, 1998; N = noncitable, W = withdrawing order, A = amending order; the 2009 order sets the pinpoint form 'Doe v. Roe, 1998 MT 12, ¶¶ 44-45, 286 Mont. 175, 989 P.2d 1312'. Montana Reports (Mont.) is the official reporter; pre-1998 form is 'Roe v. Doe (1997), 284 Mont. 301, 989 P.2d 472'. There is no intermediate appellate court. CourtListener ids from memory, unverified; no id known for the Workers' Compensation Court. Independent check 2026-10-17 fixes: M.C.A. suffix now matches (\b moved inside MCA), 'Mont. Const. Art. II, sec. N', 'Mont. R. Prof'l Conduct', and 'Rule N, Uniform District Court Rules' added. No false routes were found.

sources.title: Montana Code Annotated (MCA), current and prior editions
sources.official_status_evidence: Each section page: 'The Internet version of the Montana Code Annotated is provided as a research tool'; printed version prevails. help.html: enrolled bill on file with the Secretary of State prevails. https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/help.html
sources.coverage: MCA 2025 (current), one HTML page per section incl. constitution and the codified court rules; prior editions 2017+ in the same scheme, 1999-2015 in an older .htm scheme.

access.pattern_rules: Split the cite T-C-NNN(N) into title T, chapter C, and section number; part = section number without its last two digits, section = its last two digits. Each numeric component N becomes str(N*10) zero-padded to 4 digits (27 -> 0270, 2 -> 0020, 16 -> 0160, 21 -> 0210). A chapter with a letter (30-9A-101, 25-30A) becomes the number zero-padded to 3 digits plus the letter (009A, 030A). Examples verified 2026-10-17: 27-2-204 -> title_0270/chapter_0020/part_0020/section_0040/0270-0020-0020-0040.html; 15-30-2101 -> title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0210/section_0010/0150-0300-0210-0010.html; 30-9A-101 -> title_0300/chapter_009A/part_0010/section_0010/0300-009A-0010-0010.html; 45-5-101 (repealed stub). A wrong path returns HTTP 404 (no soft 200). Prior editions (2017 onward) use the same path under /bills/{YYYY}/mca/ (2019 verified: 'Montana Code Annotated 2019'); 1999-2015 editions use /bills/{YYYY}/mca/{T}/{C}/{T}-{C}-{NNN}.htm (seen in search results, not fetched). leg.mt.gov/bills/mca/... and archive.legmt.gov/bills/MCA/... redirect (302) to mca.legmt.gov.
access.navigation: index.html → title_TTTT/chapters_index.html → chapter_CCCC/parts_index.html (part names only) → part_PPPP/sections_index.html (lists every section number with catchline) → section page.

automation.robots_txt: www.legmt.gov/robots.txt: only GPTBot and meta-externalagent crawl-delay 10; mca.legmt.gov/robots.txt is a 404 page.
automation.notes: WebFetch returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED on both the constructed mca.legmt.gov URL and the 302 target of a search-result archive.legmt.gov URL; verified by fetch_doc.py. Pages are 0.7-16K chars, no truncation.
